## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

```{r}
storm_dates_1 <- ("2026-08-14")
storm_dates_2 <- ("2026-08-15")
storm_dates_3 <- ("2026-08-16")
storm_dates_4 <- ("2026-08-17")
after_dates_1 <- ("2026-08-18")
after_dates_2 <- ("2026-08-19")
after_dates_3 <- ("2026-08-20")
after_dates_4 <- ("2026-08-21")
baseline_dates <- seq.Date(from = as.Date("2026-08-03"), to = as.Date("2026-08-13"), by = "day")
all_dates <- c(baseline_dates, storm_dates_1, storm_dates_2, storm_dates_3, storm_dates_4, after_dates_1, after_dates_2, after_dates_3, after_dates_4)
```

```{r}
roi_hawaii <- counties(state = "HI", cb = TRUE, year = 2022) |>
  st_transform(4326) |>
  st_crop(xmin = -160.5, xmax = -154.5, ymin = 18.5, ymax = 22.5) |>
  filter(NAMELSAD != "Kalawao County") |>
  mutate(county = gsub(" County", "", NAME))
```

```{r}
pull_one_date <- function(d) {
  tryCatch({
    bm_raster(roi_sf = roi_hawaii,
              product_id = "VNP46A2",
              date = d,
              bearer = bearer,
              quality_flag_rm = 2)
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Failed for ", d, ": ", conditionMessage(e))
    NULL
  })
}

r_list <- map(all_dates, pull_one_date)
names(r_list) <- as.character(all_dates)
r_list <- compact(r_list)

message("Dates successfully pulled: ", paste(names(r_list), collapse = ", "))
message("Dates dropped (no imagery / failed): ",
        paste(setdiff(as.character(all_dates), names(r_list)), collapse = ", "))

r_all <- rast(r_list)

baseline_ok <- intersect(as.character(baseline_dates), names(r_all))
storm_ok_1 <- intersect(as.character(storm_dates_1), names(r_all))
storm_ok_2 <- intersect(as.character(storm_dates_2), names(r_all))
storm_ok_3 <- intersect(as.character(storm_dates_3), names(r_all))
storm_ok_4 <- intersect(as.character(storm_dates_4), names(r_all))
after_ok_1 <- intersect(as.character(after_dates_1), names(r_all))
after_ok_2 <- intersect(as.character(after_dates_2), names(r_all))
after_ok_3 <- intersect(as.character(after_dates_3), names(r_all))
after_ok_4 <- intersect(as.character(after_dates_4), names(r_all))


r_baseline <- r_all[[baseline_ok]]
r_storm_1 <- r_all[[storm_ok_1]]
r_storm_2 <- r_all[[storm_ok_2]]
r_storm_3 <- r_all[[storm_ok_3]]
r_storm_4 <- r_all[[storm_ok_4]]
r_after_1 <- r_all[[after_ok_1]]
r_after_2 <- r_all[[after_ok_2]]
r_after_3 <- r_all[[after_ok_3]]
r_after_4 <- r_all[[after_ok_4]]
```

```{r}
r_baseline <- terra::mask(r_baseline, roi_hawaii)
r_storm_1  <- terra::mask(r_storm_1, roi_hawaii)
r_storm_2  <- terra::mask(r_storm_2, roi_hawaii)
r_storm_3  <- terra::mask(r_storm_3, roi_hawaii)
r_storm_4  <- terra::mask(r_storm_4, roi_hawaii)
r_after_1  <- terra::mask(r_after_1, roi_hawaii)
r_after_2  <- terra::mask(r_after_2, roi_hawaii)
r_after_3  <- terra::mask(r_after_3, roi_hawaii)
r_after_4  <- terra::mask(r_after_4, roi_hawaii)

completeness_check <- tibble(
  date = c(baseline_ok, storm_ok_1, storm_ok_2, storm_ok_3, storm_ok_4, after_ok_1, after_ok_2, after_ok_3, after_ok_4),
  
  period = c(
    rep("Baseline", length(baseline_ok)), 
    rep("Storm 1", length(storm_ok_1)), 
    rep("Storm 2", length(storm_ok_2)), 
    rep("Storm 3", length(storm_ok_3)), 
    rep("Storm 4", length(storm_ok_4)), 
    rep("After 1", length(after_ok_1)),
    rep("After 2", length(after_ok_2)), 
    rep("After 3", length(after_ok_3)), 
    rep("After 4", length(after_ok_4))
  ), # <-- Added comma and closed c() properly here
  
  n_valid_pixels = c(
    sapply(seq_len(nlyr(r_baseline)), function(i) sum(!is.na(values(r_baseline[[i]])))),
    sapply(seq_len(nlyr(r_storm_1)), function(i) sum(!is.na(values(r_storm_1[[i]])))),
    sapply(seq_len(nlyr(r_storm_2)), function(i) sum(!is.na(values(r_storm_2[[i]])))),
    sapply(seq_len(nlyr(r_storm_3)), function(i) sum(!is.na(values(r_storm_3[[i]])))),
    sapply(seq_len(nlyr(r_storm_4)), function(i) sum(!is.na(values(r_storm_4[[i]])))),
    sapply(seq_len(nlyr(r_after_1)), function(i) sum(!is.na(values(r_after_1[[i]])))),
    sapply(seq_len(nlyr(r_after_2)), function(i) sum(!is.na(values(r_after_2[[i]])))),
    sapply(seq_len(nlyr(r_after_3)), function(i) sum(!is.na(values(r_after_3[[i]])))),
    sapply(seq_len(nlyr(r_after_4)), function(i) sum(!is.na(values(r_after_4[[i]]))))
  )
)

print(completeness_check)
```

```{r}
# 1. Update the function to accept the actual date vector explicitly
extract_from_local <- function(raster_stack, roi_sf, date_vector) {
  map_dfr(seq_len(nlyr(raster_stack)), function(i) {
    layer <- raster_stack[[i]]
    vals <- exact_extract(layer, roi_sf, fun = "mean")
    
    tibble(
      county   = roi_sf$county,
      date     = as.Date(date_vector[i]), # Uses your explicit date vectors safely
      ntl_mean = vals
    )
  })
}

# 2. Combine rows (Removed the duplicate Storm 1 block)
ntl_trend <- bind_rows(
  extract_from_local(r_baseline, roi_hawaii, baseline_ok) |> mutate(period = "Baseline"),
  extract_from_local(r_storm_1,  roi_hawaii, storm_ok_1)  |> mutate(period = "Storm 1"),
  extract_from_local(r_storm_2,  roi_hawaii, storm_ok_2)  |> mutate(period = "Storm 2"),
  extract_from_local(r_storm_3,  roi_hawaii, storm_ok_3)  |> mutate(period = "Storm 3"),
  extract_from_local(r_storm_4,  roi_hawaii, storm_ok_4)  |> mutate(period = "Storm 4"),
  extract_from_local(r_after_1,  roi_hawaii, after_ok_1)  |> mutate(period = "After 1"),
  extract_from_local(r_after_2,  roi_hawaii, after_ok_2)  |> mutate(period = "After 2"),
  extract_from_local(r_after_3,  roi_hawaii, after_ok_3)  |> mutate(period = "After 3"),
  extract_from_local(r_after_4,  roi_hawaii, after_ok_4)  |> mutate(period = "After 4")
)

# 3. Create a broader group for color assignment 
statewide_trend <- ntl_trend |> 
  group_by(date, period) |> 
  summarize(ntl_mean = mean(ntl_mean, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |> 
  mutate(color_group = if_else(period == "Baseline", "Baseline", "Storm and After"))

# 4. Plot using 'color_group' for the fill aesthetic instead of 'period'
ggplot(statewide_trend, aes(x = date, y = ntl_mean, fill = color_group)) + 
  geom_col() + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Baseline" = "grey70", "Storm and After" = "firebrick")) + 
  labs(
    title    = "Statewide Mean Nighttime Radiance by Day", 
    subtitle = "Comparing tracking periods before, during, and after the storm event", 
    x        = "Date", 
    y        = "Mean radiance", 
    fill     = NULL
  ) + 
  theme_minimal()

```

```{r}
# 1. Put all your raster objects into a named list
raster_list <- list(
  "Baseline" = r_baseline, "Storm 1" = r_storm_1, "Storm 2" = r_storm_2,
  "Storm 3"  = r_storm_3,  "Storm 4" = r_storm_4,  "After 1" = r_after_1,
  "After 2"  = r_after_2,  "After 3" = r_after_3,  "After 4" = r_after_4
)

# 2. Put all your date vectors into a matching list
date_list <- list(
  "Baseline" = baseline_ok, "Storm 1" = storm_ok_1, "Storm 2" = storm_ok_2,
  "Storm 3"  = storm_ok_3,  "Storm 4" = storm_ok_4,  "After 1" = after_ok_1,
  "After 2"  = after_ok_2,  "After 3" = after_ok_3,  "After 4" = after_ok_4
)

# 3. Cleanly process everything in one loop
completeness_check <- imap_dfr(raster_list, function(raster_obj, period_name) {
  
  # Calculate valid pixels safely using terra's built-in global count
  # global() is much faster and uses less memory than values()
  valid_counts <- terra::global(raster_obj, fun = function(x) sum(!is.na(x)))[, 1]
  
  tibble(
    date           = date_list[[period_name]],
    period         = period_name,
    n_valid_pixels = valid_counts
  )
})

print(completeness_check)
```

```{r}
# 1. Clean up both rasters to the study area boundary
baseline_clean <- terra::crop(baseline_mean, roi_hawaii) |> terra::mask(roi_hawaii)
storm_clean    <- terra::crop(r_storm_1, roi_hawaii)    |> terra::mask(roi_hawaii)

# 2. Resample baseline to match the exact resolution and alignment of the storm raster
# 'near' is best for categorical data, 'bilinear' is ideal for continuous imagery (like radiance)
baseline_resampled <- terra::resample(baseline_clean, storm_clean, method = "bilinear")

# 3. Extract values (they are now guaranteed to have the exact same size)
paired_values <- tibble(
  baseline = values(baseline_resampled)[, 1],
  storm_1  = values(storm_clean)[, 1]
) |> 
  filter(!is.na(baseline), !is.na(storm_1)) 

# 4. Plot the matched pixels
ggplot(paired_values, aes(x = baseline, y = storm_1)) + 
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "firebrick", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Oahu: Storm 1 vs. Baseline Radiance, Per Pixel (", storm_dates_1, ")"), 
    subtitle = "Points below the dashed line got darker; above got brighter", 
    x = "Baseline radiance", 
    y = "Storm-night 1 radiance"
  ) + 
  theme_minimal()

```

baseline_clean <- terra::crop(baseline_mean, roi_hawaii) |> terra::mask(roi_hawaii)
after4_clean   <- terra::crop(r_after_4, roi_hawaii)     |> terra::mask(roi_hawaii)

paired_recovery_final <- tibble(
  baseline = values(baseline_resampled)[, 1],
  after_4  = values(after4_clean)[, 1]

paired_recovery_final |>

    n_total          = n(),

  )

```{r map-abs-change}
# 1. Clean and align the two layers to your study area boundary
baseline_clean <- terra::crop(baseline_mean, roi_hawaii) |> terra::mask(roi_hawaii)
storm_clean    <- terra::crop(r_storm_1, roi_hawaii)    |> terra::mask(roi_hawaii)

# 2. Resample baseline to match the pixel grid structure of your storm imagery
baseline_resampled <- terra::resample(baseline_clean, storm_clean, method = "bilinear")

# 3. Calculate the absolute change (Storm minus Baseline)
abs_change <- storm_clean - baseline_resampled

# 4. Filter out very dim pixels (noise floor) to keep only meaningful changes
# Set a threshold value based on your data (e.g., keeping changes where baseline > 0.5)
# Adjust the '0.5' threshold below to fit your specific dataset's noise floor
abs_change_meaningful <- terra::mask(abs_change, baseline_resampled > 0.5, maskvalues = FALSE)


# 5. Build your map now that the object is successfully created
ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = abs_change_meaningful) +
  geom_sf(data = roi_hawaii, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low      = "darkred", 
    mid      = "white", 
    high     = "darkgreen", 
    midpoint = 0, 
    na.value = "transparent", 
    name     = "Absolute\nchange"
  ) + 
  labs(
    title    = "Oahu: Absolute Radiance Change — Dim/Medium/Bright Pixels Only", 
    subtitle = paste0("Baseline vs. Storm Night 1 (", storm_dates_1, "); Very dim pixels (noise floor) excluded"),
    x        = NULL, 
    y        = NULL 
  ) + 
  coord_sf() + 
  theme_minimal()

```
